name: The Sydney System for Performance, Classification and Reporting of Lymph Node Cytopathology
specimen: Lymph node FNA (palpation/US/EUS/EBUS), with ROSE and ancillary studies
use: Superficial and deep lymph node FNA in adults and children.
Can be combined with site-specific systems (e.g. thyroid Tg washout) for metastatic disease.
not_use: Extranodal lymphoid masses at other sites can use descriptive reporting (or WHO LN/spleen/thymus system).
Not a substitute for histology in primary lymphoma subtyping.
report_structure: Site, guidance, number of passes, ROSE
Ancillary tests performed (flow, IHC, FISH, molecular, microbiology)

adequacy.title: Performance & adequacy
items: Sydney part I covers performance: 22–27G needles, US guidance, ROSE, dedicated passes for flow cytometry (RPMI), cell block, microbiology (culture/CBNAAT) and molecular studies.
No numerical threshold; adequacy = sufficient representative, well-preserved material to answer the clinical question.
Necrotic material should prompt further passes from the periphery.

categories.name: Inadequate / Non-diagnostic
categories.definition: Insufficient, poorly preserved or obscured material, or material not representative of the lesion.

rom.source: Meta-analysis, 9 studies/13,205 cases (Acta Cytol 2024;68:13, doi 10.1159/000535797) – pooled (95% CI)

categories.management: Repeat FNA (ultrasound-guided, with ROSE) or core/excision biopsy depending on clinical suspicion.
criteria: Scant lymphoid cells/blood only; crush or air-drying artefact; necrosis only without viable cells (necrosis alone can be informative).
Material not representative of the clinically/radiologically suspicious node.

diagnoses.name: Inadequate – scant/blood only
diagnoses.final: L1: Inadequate/non-diagnostic. Insufficient lymphoid material for evaluation.
diagnoses.comment: Repeat ultrasound-guided FNA with ROSE or biopsy recommended if clinically indicated.

diagnoses.name: Non-diagnostic – necrotic material only
diagnoses.final: L1: Non-diagnostic. Necrotic material only, no viable cells.
diagnoses.comment: Differential includes tuberculosis, necrotic metastasis and lymphoma. Suggest AFB stain/CBNAAT and repeat FNA from the viable periphery or biopsy.

categories.name: Benign
categories.definition: Reactive/benign lymphoid process with polymorphous population, or specific benign diagnosis.

rom.source: Meta-analysis, 9 studies/13,205 cases (Acta Cytol 2024;68:13, doi 10.1159/000535797) – pooled (95% CI)

categories.management: Clinical follow-up; re-evaluate (repeat FNA/biopsy) if node persists or enlarges. Ancillary flow may support benign.
criteria: Polymorphous lymphoid population: small lymphocytes predominate with centrocytes, centroblasts, immunoblasts, plasma cells, tingible-body macrophages, lymphohistiocytic aggregates.
Specific benign patterns: granulomatous, suppurative, histiocytic, infectious.

diagnoses.name: Reactive lymphoid hyperplasia
diagnoses.final: L2: Benign. Reactive lymphoid hyperplasia.
diagnoses.comment: Polymorphous lymphoid population with tingible-body macrophages. Clinical follow-up recommended.

diagnoses.name: Granulomatous lymphadenitis
diagnoses.final: L2: Benign. Granulomatous lymphadenitis.
diagnoses.comment: Epithelioid granulomas ± multinucleated giant cells. Suggest ZN stain, CBNAAT/culture; differential sarcoidosis, fungal infection, cat-scratch disease.

diagnoses.name: Necrotizing granulomatous lymphadenitis consistent with tuberculosis
diagnoses.final: L2: Benign. Necrotizing granulomatous lymphadenitis, consistent with tuberculosis (AFB positive/negative).
diagnoses.comment: Caseous necrosis with epithelioid granulomas. ZN stain/CBNAAT result: [ ]. Correlate clinically.

diagnoses.name: Suppurative/acute lymphadenitis (abscess)
diagnoses.final: L2: Benign. Acute suppurative lymphadenitis.
diagnoses.comment: Neutrophils and necrotic debris; culture recommended.

diagnoses.name: Histiocytic necrotizing lymphadenitis (Kikuchi–Fujimoto)
diagnoses.final: L2: Benign. Features consistent with histiocytic necrotizing lymphadenitis (Kikuchi–Fujimoto).
diagnoses.comment: Karyorrhectic debris, crescentic histiocytes and plasmacytoid dendritic cells without neutrophils; exclude SLE.

diagnoses.name: Rosai–Dorfman disease
diagnoses.final: L2: Benign. Features consistent with Rosai–Dorfman disease.
diagnoses.comment: Large histiocytes with emperipolesis; S100+, CD68/CD163+, OCT2+, CD1a−.

diagnoses.name: Dermatopathic lymphadenopathy
diagnoses.final: L2: Benign. Reactive lymphadenopathy with dermatopathic features.
diagnoses.comment: Langerhans cells/histiocytes with melanin pigment; correlate with skin disease; exclude mycosis fungoides if suspected.

diagnoses.name: Infectious mononucleosis / viral lymphadenitis
diagnoses.final: L2: Benign. Reactive lymphoid hyperplasia with immunoblastic proliferation, compatible with viral (e.g. EBV) lymphadenitis.
diagnoses.comment: Monospot/EBV serology recommended; immunoblasts can mimic lymphoma.

diagnoses.name: Toxoplasma lymphadenitis
diagnoses.final: L2: Benign. Reactive lymphadenitis with microgranulomas (small epithelioid clusters), compatible with toxoplasmosis.
diagnoses.comment: Toxoplasma serology recommended.

diagnoses.name: Sarcoidosis
diagnoses.final: L2: Benign. Non-necrotizing granulomatous lymphadenitis; sarcoidosis is a consideration after exclusion of infection.
diagnoses.comment: Exclude tuberculosis and fungal infection (ZN/GMS stains, CBNAAT, culture); correlate with serum ACE, calcium and imaging.

diagnoses.name: Fungal lymphadenitis (histoplasma, cryptococcus)
diagnoses.final: L2: Benign. Granulomatous lymphadenitis with fungal organisms (specify).
diagnoses.comment: GMS/PAS stains, culture.

diagnoses.name: Benign non-lymphoid (branchial cleft cyst, lipoma) – sampled as 'node'
diagnoses.final: L2: Benign. [Specify, e.g. contents of branchial cleft cyst].
diagnoses.comment: Squamous cyst in adults >40 years: exclude cystic metastatic HPV-associated SCC (p16/HPV testing).

categories.name: Atypical (cells of undetermined significance / atypical lymphoid cells of uncertain significance)
categories.definition: Atypical cells (lymphoid or non-lymphoid) insufficient for suspicious; or limited material/ancillary tests not available.

rom.source: Meta-analysis, 9 studies/13,205 cases (Acta Cytol 2024;68:13, doi 10.1159/000535797) – pooled (95% CI)

categories.management: Repeat FNA with flow cytometry/cell block, or core/excision biopsy.
criteria: Predominantly small lymphocytes with a minor atypical population; possible low-grade lymphoma (e.g. follicular, MZL) but not confirmed.
Mixed population with increased large cells or atypical large cells; Hodgkin-like cells too few.
Few atypical non-lymphoid cells (carcinoma/melanoma not confirmed).

diagnoses.name: Atypical lymphoid cells of uncertain significance (ALUS)
diagnoses.final: L3: Atypical lymphoid cells of uncertain significance.
diagnoses.comment: Lymphoid population with atypical features insufficient for suspicion of lymphoma. Flow cytometry/IHC on repeat FNA, or excision biopsy recommended.

diagnoses.name: Atypical cells of undetermined significance (non-lymphoid, AUS)
diagnoses.final: L3: Atypical cells of undetermined significance.
diagnoses.comment: Few atypical cells of uncertain lineage; repeat FNA with cell block or biopsy recommended.

categories.name: Suspicious for malignancy
categories.definition: Features suggestive of lymphoma or metastatic malignancy but insufficient for definitive diagnosis; ancillary tests not available/inconclusive.

rom.source: Meta-analysis, 9 studies/13,205 cases (Acta Cytol 2024;68:13, doi 10.1159/000535797) – pooled (95% CI)

categories.management: Excision/core biopsy with ancillary studies; for metastasis, repeat FNA/cell block or biopsy.
criteria: Monomorphous lymphoid population (small or large) without flow/IHC confirmation.
Few Reed–Sternberg/Hodgkin cells in an appropriate background.
Few atypical epithelial/melanocytic cells suspicious for metastasis.

diagnoses.name: Suspicious for lymphoma (NHL)
diagnoses.final: L4: Suspicious for malignancy – suspicious for non-Hodgkin lymphoma.
diagnoses.comment: Monotonous lymphoid population; flow cytometry/IHC and excision biopsy are recommended for classification.

diagnoses.name: Suspicious for Hodgkin lymphoma
diagnoses.final: L4: Suspicious for malignancy – suspicious for classic Hodgkin lymphoma.
diagnoses.comment: Occasional large atypical binucleate/mononuclear cells in a reactive background of eosinophils, plasma cells and histiocytes. Excision biopsy with CD30/CD15/PAX5 (weak) IHC recommended.

diagnoses.name: Suspicious for metastatic malignancy
diagnoses.final: L4: Suspicious for malignancy – suspicious for metastatic [carcinoma/melanoma].
diagnoses.comment: Repeat FNA with cell block or biopsy recommended.

categories.name: Malignant
categories.definition: Unequivocal malignancy; specify lymphoma (with subtype where ancillary tests allow) or metastatic tumour.

rom.source: Meta-analysis, 9 studies/13,205 cases (Acta Cytol 2024;68:13, doi 10.1159/000535797) – pooled (95% CI)

categories.management: Lymphoma: excision/core biopsy usually needed for WHO subtype unless FNA + flow/IHC/FISH sufficient (e.g. recurrence, staging). Metastasis: work up primary; cell block for IHC/biomarkers.
criteria: Metastatic carcinoma: cohesive non-lymphoid malignant cells; squamous, glandular, small cell, undifferentiated patterns.
NHL confirmed by flow cytometry (light-chain restriction/aberrant phenotype) ± IHC/FISH.
Classic Hodgkin lymphoma with diagnostic RS cells and IHC.

diagnoses.name: Metastatic squamous cell carcinoma
diagnoses.final: L5: Malignant. Metastatic squamous cell carcinoma.
diagnoses.comment: p16/HPV ISH recommended for cervical nodes (oropharyngeal primary); search for primary.

diagnoses.name: Metastatic adenocarcinoma
diagnoses.final: L5: Malignant. Metastatic adenocarcinoma.
diagnoses.comment: IHC on cell block to suggest primary.

diagnoses.name: Metastatic papillary thyroid carcinoma
diagnoses.final: L5: Malignant. Metastatic papillary thyroid carcinoma.
diagnoses.comment: Thyroglobulin washout/IHC (TTF1, Tg) supports.

diagnoses.name: Metastatic small cell / neuroendocrine carcinoma
diagnoses.final: L5: Malignant. Metastatic small cell carcinoma.
diagnoses.comment: Small cells with nuclear moulding, fine chromatin and crush artefact; confirm with synaptophysin/chromogranin/INSM1 and TTF1 on cell block; lung is the usual primary.

diagnoses.name: Metastatic undifferentiated / lymphoepithelial (nasopharyngeal) carcinoma
diagnoses.final: L5: Malignant. Metastatic undifferentiated (lymphoepithelial) carcinoma.
diagnoses.comment: EBER ISH recommended (nasopharyngeal primary).

diagnoses.name: Metastatic melanoma
diagnoses.final: L5: Malignant. Metastatic melanoma.
diagnoses.comment: SOX10/S100/HMB45/Melan-A.

diagnoses.name: Metastatic germ cell tumour (seminoma etc.)
diagnoses.final: L5: Malignant. Metastatic germ cell tumour.
diagnoses.comment: OCT3/4, SALL4, PLAP/CD117; serum markers.

diagnoses.name: Diffuse large B-cell lymphoma
diagnoses.final: L5: Malignant. Non-Hodgkin lymphoma, large B-cell type (flow/IHC confirmed).
diagnoses.comment: Excision biopsy suggested for cell-of-origin, MYC/BCL2/BCL6 FISH.

diagnoses.name: Low-grade B-cell lymphoma (CLL/SLL, follicular, mantle, marginal zone)
diagnoses.final: L5: Malignant. Low-grade B-cell non-Hodgkin lymphoma, [subtype if determined].
diagnoses.comment: Flow cytometry: [immunophenotype]. Grading of follicular lymphoma requires histology.

diagnoses.name: Burkitt lymphoma / high-grade B-cell lymphoma
diagnoses.final: L5: Malignant. High-grade B-cell lymphoma, consistent with Burkitt lymphoma.
diagnoses.comment: MYC FISH and urgent oncology referral.

diagnoses.name: Lymphoblastic lymphoma
diagnoses.final: L5: Malignant. Lymphoblastic lymphoma (TdT+).
diagnoses.comment: Medium-sized blasts with fine chromatin; flow cytometry for B/T lineage (CD34, TdT, CD19/cCD3). Urgent haemato-oncology referral; often mediastinal mass in T-LBL.

diagnoses.name: T-cell lymphoma (PTCL, ALCL)
diagnoses.final: L5: Malignant. T-cell lymphoma [ALCL, ALK+/−, PTCL].
diagnoses.comment: Histology for classification.

diagnoses.name: Classic Hodgkin lymphoma
diagnoses.final: L5: Malignant. Classic Hodgkin lymphoma.
diagnoses.comment: RS/Hodgkin cells (CD30+, CD15+, PAX5 weak, CD45−) in a mixed background; excision biopsy for subtyping.

diagnoses.name: Plasma cell neoplasm / myeloid sarcoma
diagnoses.final: L5: Malignant. [Plasmacytoma / myeloid sarcoma].
diagnoses.comment: Plasma cell neoplasm: CD138, kappa/lambda, SPEP/free light chains. Myeloid sarcoma: MPO, CD117, CD34, lysozyme; bone marrow evaluation recommended.

extra.title: Ancillary tests
items: Flow cytometry: light-chain restriction, CD5/CD10/CD23/CD200/FMC7 (B-cell), T-cell aberrancy; best on fresh RPMI material.
Cell block IHC: CD20/CD3/CD10/BCL2/BCL6/MUM1/cyclin D1/SOX11/Ki-67, CD30/CD15/PAX5, TdT; epithelial/melanocytic panels.
FISH/molecular: MYC, BCL2, BCL6, CCND1; IGH/TCR clonality; EBER ISH; HPV.

references: Al-Abbadi MA, Barroca H, Bode-Lesniewska B, et al. A Proposal for the Performance, Classification, and Reporting of Lymph Node Fine-Needle Aspiration Cytopathology: The Sydney System. Acta Cytol. 2020;64(4):306–322.
